title: Scoped Security Acceptance & Incident Playbook for SAML Replay, Key Rotation, and RBAC Drift
creator: Aisha Verma
description: This PRD+playbook defines the acceptance criteria, test scenarios, and incident runbook for three cross-cutting security controls required for Private/VPC deployments: 1) SAML assertion integrity and replay protection, 2) cross-region key rotation and emergency HSM fallback, and 3) RBAC drift detection and automated remediation cues. Goal: provide deterministic sign-off criteria for Compliance and Customer Onboarding teams, plus on-call runbook steps for any security incidents that touch auth, keys, or RBAC policies.
scope_changes: Initial scope included only SSO and KMS acceptance; expanded to include RBAC drift detection after risk review on 2025-02-20.
Removed plan for automated key escrow transfer between regions—now a manual operator procedure in runbook due to legal review (see decision log).
Added explicit retention and audit window acceptance criteria for operator key usage logs following customer feedback.
acceptance_criteria: SAML: IdP-initiated and SP-initiated flows pass end-to-end integration tests with signed assertions verified and recorded in audit logs.
SAML Replay Protection: All assertion IDs are checked against a 24-hour anti-replay store; attempts are logged and generate an alert with severity mapping.
KMS/HSM: Routine key rotation can be executed without service interruption; a rollback path exists via HSM-signed attestations and documented operator steps.
Cross-region rotation: Rotation job completes within defined maintenance window (<10 minutes for active shards) in automated dry-run mode; manual fallback documented.
RBAC: Policy drift detection alerts when a high-privilege binding is created outside RBAC pipeline; a one-click revoke link appears in Console with trace to PR/approval.
Auditability: All SSO/KMS/RBAC operations create immutable audit events forwarded to customer audit sinks and retained for minimum 90 days as part of acceptance tests.
Performance: Acceptance tests impose no more than 5% p99 latency increase on steady-state inference requests when audit forwarding is enabled.
signoff_checklist: Security Review completed and signed by Security Engineering lead (signature: S. Ortega).
Compliance checklist validated against SOC2 and customer-specific contract clauses (doc: Confluence > Compliance Evidence).
End-to-end smoke tests for SAML, KMS rotation, and RBAC scenarios green in staging for 72 hours.
Operator runbook validated by on-call rotation and incident walkthrough complete (recording attached).
Customer onboarding checklist updated with manual escalation path and contact points.
Release readiness: telemetry dashboards, alert pages, and runbooks linked from release notes.
test_plan: OOB Integration: Run scripted IdP/ SP flows against test IdP (OKTA dev tenant) and verify assertion signatures and attribute mapping.
Replay test: Reuse a valid assertion ID within 24 hours to ensure system blocks and records proper alert metric 'saml.replay.attempt'.
Chaos rotation: Trigger a key rotation in a non-prod region with simulated failover to HSM backup to validate continuity plan.
RBAC drift injection: Create a high-privilege binding via API bypass and verify detection, alerting, and Console revoke link functionality.
Audit integrity: Verify signed audit bundle exported to customer sink contains complete operation trace for a sample of events.
Load impact: Run a 60-minute load test with audit forwarding enabled and assert token generation p99 latency remains within 5% of baseline.
runbook_steps: Incident triage: On alert (saml.replay.attempt or rbac.drift.detected), set incident priority to Sev2 and tag 'auth-key'.
Containment: Disable new SAML assertions by toggling IdP handshake TTL to 0 in staging proxies, verify assertion rejection within 60s.
Key isolation: If rotation failed with sign mismatch, move affected key to 'isolated' HSM partition and re-route requests to last-known-good key version.
Recovery: If RBAC compromise detected, execute console revoke link for implicated binding, rotate damaged API client credentials, and force session invalidation.
Forensic capture: Export signed audit bundle, include assertion samples and KMS operation logs; place in secure evidence bucket with restricted ACLs.
Communication: Notify Compliance and affected customers within SLA window; escalate to Privacy/legal for any PII/PI leakage.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Automated cross-region key escrow could violate customer contracts. Mitigation: retain manual escrow process and add explicit consent in onboarding flow.
Risk: Replay store size growth under heavy SSO load. Mitigation: implement TTL-based LRU store and metrics to trigger capacity autoscaling.
Risk: RBAC alerts produce false positives during bulk provisioning. Mitigation: implement a grace window for pipeline-originated bindings and label-sourced exceptions.
decisions: Decision: Keep key escrow manual after legal review (2025-02-25) to avoid cross-border custody complications.
Decision: Use a 24-hour anti-replay window as the default for Private customers, configurable per-customer in acceptance of risk and latency tradeoffs.
Decision: RBAC remediation should be operator-triggered with a one-click Console action, not fully automated, due to potential business-impacting removals.
